result.title: Saga: an in silico ontology for a multimodal patient world model
result.summary: Simulating an individual's disease course requires connecting patient history to future events, clinical timing and disease morphology. Longitudinal prediction and multimodal representations exploit this information, but organizing future readouts around a common patient state and advancing trajectories without real intermediate observations remain central challenges. Here we introduce Saga, a multimodal patient world model that learns a shared state from patient histories to predict clinical events and generate multimodal images. Generated events and times are appended to the history and re-encoded to advance prediction. We studied 461,370 patients with 12 cancer types across 112 centres. Modality-specific paired evaluations linked future images to observed follow-up. With historical images held fixed, removing patient conditioning reduced event F1 from 0.716 to 0.591 and increased lesion-burden error from 11.8% to 21.3%. In free rollouts, eight-step event F1 was 0.672, compared with 0.553 for a longitudinal Transformer evaluated from the same origins, and timing error was lower by 8.7 days. In the internal test set, one-year progression AUROC was 0.882, with values of 0.871 and 0.856 in temporal and geographical external evaluations. These results show that shared patient states connect future phenotypes across observational scales with event-driven trajectory progression, sustaining comparative predictive advantages during rollout and discrimination in external clinical evaluation. Saga makes patient-level disease simulation a multimodal prediction task that can be tested against observed follow-up.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Saga 多模态患者世界模型：从病史学习共享病人状态，据此预测临床事件并生成多模态图像，再把生成的事件与时间回写重编码以推进轨迹，并在 46 万余例、12 种癌症队列上做同期与外部验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享 latent 状态 + 生成事件回填再编码」的自回归 rollout 与对照随访的评价方式，可能为 LVR 的状态更新、自生成轨迹训练与停止推进提供类比线索，但该研究属于医学影像与疾病轨迹预测；它能否迁移到 VLM 推理尚待核查。
